title: Video Action Replay — Watch & Do CAD/CAM from Videos
brief: Build a complete pipeline that watches CAD/CAM tutorial videos, extracts action sequences, maps them to executable CAD operations, and replays those actions via CadQuery (programmatic) or Playwright (GUI automation). The system should be able to 'learn by watching' — not just extract knowledge, but reproduce the demonstrated work.

phases.title: Video Action Recognition
phases.description: Extend VideoLearningEngine to extract structured action sequences from video, not just knowledge. Each keyframe is analyzed for: what UI element is being interacted with, what operation is being performed, what parameters are visible.

units.title: VideoActionExtractorEngine — Frame-to-Action Recognition
steps: Create src/engines/VideoActionExtractorEngine.ts
Method: extractActions(videoPath, options) — extends VideoLearningEngine pipeline

For each keyframe pair (before/after), use Claude Vision to identify: (1) what changed between frames, (2) what CAD/CAM operation was performed, (3) what parameters/values are visible on screen, (4) what tool/menu was used
Output: ActionSequence[] — ordered list of { timestamp, action_type, operation, parameters, ui_context, screenshot_ref }

Action types taxonomy: 'sketch_create', 'sketch_constraint', 'extrude', 'revolve', 'fillet', 'chamfer', 'cut', 'pattern', 'mirror', 'shell', 'loft', 'sweep', 'assembly_mate', 'toolpath_create', 'parameter_set', 'menu_navigate', 'view_change'
Use adaptive keyframe extraction — more frames during action sequences, fewer during pauses
Include OCR for parameter values visible in UI (dimensions, angles, depths)
Write 15+ tests covering: action type identification, parameter extraction, sequence ordering, OCR accuracy, edge cases (fast actions, dark UI)
exit_conditions: Can process a sample video and output structured ActionSequence[]
Correctly identifies at least 5 action types from test frames

units.title: ActionSequenceValidator — Verify and Clean Action Sequences
steps: Create validation/cleaning layer for extracted action sequences
Method: validateSequence(actions) — check logical consistency (can't fillet before creating a solid, can't extrude without a sketch)
Method: deduplicateActions(actions) — remove redundant view changes, repeated menu navigations
Method: inferMissingParams(actions) — if OCR missed a dimension, infer from geometry context
Method: classifyDifficulty(actions) — rate 1-5 how complex the sequence is
Build a CAD operation dependency graph: sketch → extrude → fillet → chamfer (topological sort)
Write 10+ tests

units.title: CADOperationTaxonomy — Standardized Operation Catalog
steps: Create a comprehensive taxonomy mapping video-observed operations to standardized CAD API calls

Cover all major CAD operations: 2D sketching (line, arc, circle, rectangle, spline, trim, offset, mirror, pattern), 3D modeling (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, shell, fillet, chamfer, boolean, draft, rib, hole), assembly (mate, constrain, pattern), CAM (toolpath, operation, setup)
Map each operation to: (1) CadQuery Python call, (2) Playwright GUI actions for Fusion 360/OnShape/FreeCAD, (3) required parameters with types/units/defaults
Include visual signatures — what each operation looks like in different CAD software UIs
Write 8+ tests
exit_conditions: 40+ CAD operations cataloged with both CadQuery and GUI mappings
Each operation has required/optional parameters defined

phases.title: Action-to-Code Translation
phases.description: Translate validated action sequences into executable code — either CadQuery Python scripts or Playwright automation scripts.

units.title: CadQueryCodeGenerator — Actions to CadQuery Python
steps: Create src/engines/CadQueryCodeGeneratorEngine.ts
Method: generateScript(actions: ActionSequence[]) → string (Python CadQuery code)
For each action in sequence, emit the corresponding CadQuery call: sketch().rect(w,h).extrude(d).fillet(r)...
Handle variable naming, workplane selection, coordinate transforms
Include comments in generated code linking back to video timestamps
Support parametric generation — extract dimensions as variables at top of script
Method: generateStepByStep(actions) → { step: number, code: string, description: string }[]
Validate generated code syntax (parse check before execution)
Integrate with existing cad-engine/code_gen.py patterns
Write 12+ tests: simple extrude, sketch+extrude+fillet, multi-body, parametric, comments
exit_conditions: Generates valid CadQuery Python for 10+ operation types
Generated code executes without error in CadQuery

units.title: PlaywrightAutomationGenerator — Actions to GUI Script
steps: Create src/engines/PlaywrightAutomationEngine.ts
Method: generateGUIScript(actions, target_software) → PlaywrightAction[]
Target software profiles: FreeCAD (desktop via Playwright), OnShape (web), Fusion 360 (web panel), TinkerCAD (web)
For each CAD action, generate Playwright calls: navigate to menu, click tool, enter parameters, confirm
Handle wait-for-element patterns (CAD UIs are async — geometry computation takes time)
Include screenshot verification after each major action
Method: executeWithVerification(actions, browser) — run actions and verify each step matches expected result
Use Playwright MCP tools: browser_click, browser_fill_form, browser_snapshot, browser_wait_for
Write 10+ tests (mock Playwright actions, verify correct click targets)
exit_conditions: Generates valid Playwright scripts for at least 2 target CAD systems

units.title: HybridExecutionEngine — Route to Best Execution Path
steps: Create routing engine that decides: CadQuery (fast, scriptable) vs Playwright (GUI, any software)
Decision logic: if all operations are supported by CadQuery → use CadQuery; if target is specific CAM software → use Playwright; if mixed → use CadQuery for modeling + Playwright for CAM
Method: planExecution(actions, preferences) → ExecutionPlan with ordered steps and execution targets
Method: executeHybrid(plan) — orchestrate both CadQuery and Playwright in correct order
Write 8+ tests
exit_conditions: Routes to correct execution engine based on operation types

phases.title: Execution & Feedback Loop
phases.description: Execute generated code, verify results match the video, and handle errors with intelligent retry.

units.title: ExecutionVerificationEngine — Run and Compare
steps: Create src/engines/ExecutionVerificationEngine.ts
Method: executeAndVerify(code, expected_keyframe) — run CadQuery code, capture result, compare to video keyframe
Geometry comparison: export STEP/STL, compare bounding box, volume, face count against expected
Visual comparison: render result, use Claude Vision to compare with video keyframe — 'does this look like the expected result?'
Tolerance-based matching: allow 5-10% dimensional deviation (video extraction isn't pixel-perfect)
Method: diagnoseFailure(expected, actual) — identify what went wrong (wrong dimension, missing feature, wrong sequence)
Write 10+ tests
exit_conditions: Can execute CadQuery code and compare result geometry
Visual comparison gives meaningful similarity score

units.title: AdaptiveRetryEngine — Self-Correcting Execution
steps: Create intelligent retry logic when execution doesn't match expected result
Method: retryWithCorrection(failedStep, diagnosis, context) — modify code based on diagnosis
Correction strategies: adjust dimensions (±10%), try alternative operation sequence, use different CadQuery API (e.g., box vs extrude), add/remove intermediate steps
Use Claude to reason about corrections: 'the fillet failed because the edge doesn't exist — the extrude direction may be wrong'
Maximum 3 retry attempts before flagging for human review
Method: learnFromCorrection(original, corrected) — store successful corrections as patterns for future videos
Write 8+ tests
exit_conditions: Successfully corrects at least 50% of first-attempt failures

units.title: ProgressTrackerEngine — Step-by-Step Execution Display
steps: Create progress tracking that shows: which video step we're on, what action is being performed, current result vs expected
Method: trackProgress(plan, currentStep) → ProgressReport with visual indicators
Include: step number, video timestamp, action description, status (pending/executing/passed/failed/retrying), screenshot comparison
Support pause/resume — user can stop at any step, inspect result, then continue
Write 6+ tests
exit_conditions: Shows clear progress through action sequence

phases.title: Interactive Learning Mode
phases.description: Allow the user to guide the system through a video tutorial interactively — pause, explain, correct, and teach.

units.title: InteractiveLearningSessionEngine — Guided Video Following
steps: Create src/engines/InteractiveLearningSessionEngine.ts
Method: startSession(videoPath, options) — begin interactive learning from a video
Workflow: (1) analyze first segment, (2) show extracted actions, (3) ask user to confirm/correct, (4) execute confirmed actions, (5) verify result, (6) proceed to next segment
Support user corrections: 'that dimension should be 25mm not 35mm', 'skip this step', 'the operation is a revolve not an extrude'
Method: askQuestion(context) — generate clarifying questions when uncertain: 'I see a fillet being applied — is the radius approximately 3mm?'
Store session corrections as training data for improving future extractions
Write 8+ tests
exit_conditions: User corrections modify the action sequence

units.title: KnowledgeTransferEngine — Learn Patterns Across Videos
steps: Create engine that accumulates learning across multiple video sessions
Method: recordPattern(videoId, actions, corrections) — store what worked and what needed correction
Method: suggestFromHistory(currentAction) — when extracting new video, suggest parameters based on similar past actions

Build a growing library of: operation signatures (what a fillet looks like across different CAD UIs), parameter ranges (typical fillet radii, extrude depths), correction patterns (common OCR errors, common misidentifications)
Method: getConfidence(action) — rate 0-1 how confident the system is in this extraction based on historical accuracy
Write 8+ tests
exit_conditions: Confidence improves with more videos processed

phases.title: Integration & Slash Commands
phases.description: Wire everything into PRISM dispatchers, create user-facing slash commands, and end-to-end testing.

units.title: Dispatcher Wiring + Action Schemas
steps: Create action schemas for all new engines
Wire to cadDispatcher or create new videoActionDispatcher
Actions: video_extract_actions, video_generate_cadquery, video_generate_playwright, video_execute_replay, video_verify_result, video_interactive_session, video_learn_pattern
Update calcDispatcher ACTIONS array and switch cases
Write 5+ integration tests
exit_conditions: All actions accessible via MCP tools

units.title: Slash Commands: /video-replay and /video-follow
steps: Create ~/.claude/commands/video-replay.md — fully autonomous: give video path, get CAD model
Create ~/.claude/commands/video-follow.md — interactive: step through video with user, learning as you go
Update SLASH_COMMANDS.md
Each command: (1) validates video exists + FFmpeg available, (2) runs pipeline, (3) reports results with screenshots
exit_conditions: Both slash commands created and documented

units.title: End-to-End Test: Simple Box Tutorial
steps: Create a test video (screen recording) of making a simple box with fillet in FreeCAD or CadQuery
Run the full pipeline: video → actions → CadQuery code → execute → verify
Verify: output STEP file has correct dimensions, 12 edges (box) with 4 filleted
Document the E2E test as a reference for future videos
Write the E2E test as a vitest integration test (skipped by default, run with --e2e flag)
exit_conditions: Full pipeline works end-to-end on test video
Output geometry matches expected within 10% tolerance
